subject: Chemistry
name: Chemistry Paper 3 (Extended)
description: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry Paper 3 (Extended), May/June 2006. Covers transition elements and iron extraction, metal reactivity series, acids and electrical conductivity, Group IV elements and allotropes, the Contact Process and equilibrium, and organic chemistry with cracking and alkenes.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Iron is a transition element. Which of the following statements about transition elements are correct? Tick three boxes.
options: The metals are highly coloured e.g. yellow, green, blue.
The metals have low melting points.
The elements and their compounds are often used as catalysts.
They have more than one oxidation state.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Iron is a transition element. (i) In which Period in the Periodic Table is iron to be found? (ii) Use the Periodic Table to work out the number of protons and the number of neutrons in one atom of iron.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Iron is extracted in a blast furnace. The list below gives some of the substances used or formed in the extraction: carbon monoxide, coke, iron ore, limestone, slag. (i) Which substance is a mineral containing largely calcium carbonate? (ii) Which substance is formed when impurities in the ore react with calcium oxide? (iii) Which substance is also called hematite?

parts.label: d
parts.question: State two functions of the coke used in the blast furnace.
keywords: reacts with oxygen to form CO2

parts.label: e
parts.question: Most of the iron is converted into mild steel or stainless steel. Give one use for each. mild steel: ............ stainless steel: ............

questions.topic: Metal Reactivity Series and Group I Metals

parts.label: a
parts.question: Some reactions of metals W, X, Y and Z are given in a table. (metal W: A few bubbles form slowly in cold water, vigorous reaction with dilute HCl. metal X: Vigorous reaction with cold water, explosive reaction with dilute HCl. metal Y: No reaction with water or HCl. metal Z: Does not react with cold water, hot metal reacts with steam, steady fizzing with HCl.) Arrange these metals in order of reactivity: most reactive ...... ...... ...... least reactive.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Which of these metals could be (i) magnesium, (ii) copper?

parts.label: c
parts.question: The equation for the reaction of X with cold water is given below: 2X(s) + 2H2O(l) → 2XOH(aq) + H2(g). (i) Describe the test you would use to show that the gas evolved is hydrogen. (ii) How could you show that the water contained a compound of the type XOH? (iii) In which group of the Periodic Table does metal X belong? (iv) The ore of X is its chloride. Suggest how metal X could be extracted from its chloride.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Four bottles were known to contain aqueous ammonia, dilute hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide solution and vinegar, which is dilute ethanoic acid. The bottles had lost their labels. The pH values of the four solutions were 1, 4, 10 and 13. Complete the table: aqueous ammonia pH ..., dilute hydrochloric acid pH ..., sodium hydroxide solution pH ..., vinegar pH ...

parts.label: b
parts.question: The following apparatus was set up to investigate the electrical conductivity of dilute acids (carbon electrodes in dilute sulphuric acid, bulb/lamp, bubbles of oxygen at anode and hydrogen at cathode). Dilute sulphuric acid is a strong acid. If it was replaced by a weak acid, what two differences in the observations would you expect to make?

parts.label: c
parts.question: When nitric acid is added to water the following reaction occurs: HNO3 + H2O → NO3– + H3O+. Give the name and the formula of the particle which is transferred from nitric acid to water.

parts.label: d
parts.question: This question is concerned with the following oxides: aluminium oxide Al2O3, calcium oxide CaO, carbon dioxide CO2, carbon monoxide CO, magnesium oxide MgO, sulphur dioxide SO2. (i) Which of the above oxides will react with hydrochloric acid but not with aqueous sodium hydroxide? (ii) Which of the above oxides will react with aqueous sodium hydroxide but not with hydrochloric acid? (iii) Which of the above oxides will react both with hydrochloric acid and with aqueous sodium hydroxide? (iv) Which of the above oxides will react neither with hydrochloric acid nor with aqueous sodium hydroxide?

questions.topic: Group IV Elements: Diamond, Graphite and Dioxides

parts.label: a
parts.question: The first three elements in Group IV are carbon, silicon, germanium. The element germanium has a diamond-type structure. Describe the structure of germanium. A diagram is acceptable.
keywords: each Ge bonded to 4 Ge atoms

parts.label: b
parts.question: Unlike diamond, graphite is soft and is a good conductor of electricity. (i) Explain why graphite has these properties. (ii) Give a use of graphite that depends on one of these properties.
keywords: each C has 3 bonds so one free electron per atom

parts.label: c
parts.question: Carbon dioxide and silicon(IV) oxide have similar formulae but different types of structure. (i) Give the formulae of these oxides. (ii) How are their structures different?

parts.label: d
parts.question: All these elements form compounds with hydrogen called hydrides. The saturated hydrides of carbon are the alkanes. Predict the formula of the hydride of germanium which contains two germanium atoms.

questions.topic: The Contact Process and Chemical Equilibrium

parts.label: a
parts.question: Sulphuric acid is made by the Contact process in the following sequence of reactions: sulphur → sulphur dioxide → sulphur trioxide → sulphuric acid. (i) How is sulphur dioxide made from sulphur? (ii) Sulphur dioxide has other uses. Why is it used in the manufacture of paper? (iii) How does it preserve food?

parts.label: b
parts.question: The equation for a stage of the Contact process is 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3. The percentage of sulphur trioxide in the equilibrium mixture varies with temperature. (i) How does the percentage of sulphur trioxide in the equilibrium mixture vary as the temperature increases? Circle the correct answer: increases / stays the same / decreases. (ii) Is the forward reaction 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3 exothermic or endothermic? Give a reason for your choice. (iii) Explain, mentioning both rate and percentage yield, why the temperature used in the Contact process is 450°C. (iv) Describe how the sulphur trioxide is changed into concentrated sulphuric acid.
keywords: SO3 percentage decreases as T increases
450°C gives reasonable rate and acceptable yield

questions.topic: Exothermic Reactions, Nuclear Fuels and Electrochemical Cells

parts.label: a
parts.question: Exothermic reactions produce heat energy. An important fuel is methane, natural gas. The equation for its combustion is as follows: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O. (i) In chemical reactions bonds are broken and new bonds are formed. Using this reaction give an example of a bond that is broken, a bond that is formed. (ii) Explain, using the idea of bonds forming and breaking, why this reaction is exothermic, that is it produces heat energy.
keywords: energy released forming bonds greater than energy absorbed breaking bonds

parts.label: b
parts.question: Some radioactive isotopes are used as nuclear fuels. (i) Give the symbol and the nucleon number of an isotope that is used as a nuclear fuel. (ii) Give another use of radioactive isotopes.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Cell reactions are both exothermic and redox. They produce electrical energy as well as heat energy. (i) The diagram shows a simple cell: iron electrode and zinc electrode in dilute sulphuric acid, with voltmeter. Bubbles of hydrogen form at the iron electrode and the zinc electrode becomes thinner. Which substance in this cell is the reductant and which ion is the oxidant? (ii) How could the voltage of this cell be increased? (iii) What is the important large scale use, relating to iron and steel, of this type of cell reaction?
keywords: replace Fe with less reactive metal
use electrodes further apart in reactivity series

questions.topic: Cracking, Alkanes, Alkenes and Percentage Yield

parts.label: a
parts.question: The fractional distillation of crude oil usually produces large quantities of the heavier fractions. The market demand is for the lighter fractions and for the more reactive alkenes. The heavier fractions are cracked to form smaller alkanes and alkenes as in the following example: C8H18 → C4H10 + C4H8 (octane → butane + butenes). (i) Write a different equation for the cracking of octane. C8H18 → ............ + ............ (ii) The cracking of octane can produce isomers with the molecular formula C4H8. Draw the structural formulae of two of these isomers.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Alkanes undergo substitution reactions with chlorine. (i) Give the essential condition for the reaction between chlorine and butane. (ii) What type of reaction is this? (iii) This reaction produces a mixture of products that contain four carbon atoms per molecule. Give the names of two products.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Alkenes are more reactive than alkanes and are used to make a range of organic chemicals. Propene, CH3–CH=CH2, is made by cracking. Give the structural formula of the addition product when propene reacts with the following. (i) water, (ii) bromine.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Propene reacts with hydrogen iodide to form 2-iodopropane. CH3−CH=CH2 + HI → CH3−CHI−CH3. 1.4 g of propene produced 4.0g of 2-iodopropane. Calculate the percentage yield. moles of CH3–CH=CH2 reacted = ...... maximum moles of CH3–CHI–CH3 that could be formed = ...... mass of one mole of CH3–CHI–CH3 = 170g. maximum mass of 2-iodopropane that could be formed = ...... percentage yield = ...... %
